title: The article and adjectives
topic: the article הַ־; the adjective after the noun and its agreement; זֶה / זֹאת
why: The article הַ, the adjective placed after the noun, and its agreement: everything you need to describe a house, a city or people. You also learn to tell "the big house" apart from "the house is big," just before the unit review.

{"lessons": ["

The article: הַ

Hebrew has just one article, הַ (ha), which means \"the.\" It is glued to the front of the word. And there is no word for \"a / an\": \"a house\" is simply בַּיִת.

Without articleWith articleMeaning
בַּיִת bayitהַבַּיִת ha-bayita house / the house
דִּירָה diraהַדִּירָה ha-diraan apartment / the apartment
סְטוּדֶנְט studentהַסְּטוּדֶנְט ha-studenta student / the student
אִישׁ ishהָאִישׁ ha-isha man / the man
עִיר irהָעִיר ha-ira city / the city
רְחוֹב rekhovהָרְחוֹב ha-rekhova street / the street

Do you see the dot that appears in the letter after הַ (הַדִּירָה, הַסְּטוּדֶנְט)? Before א, ע and ר, which don't take it, the article is written הָ. Before ה and ח, it usually stays הַ, without a dot: הַחֶדֶר (the room). In every case, it's pronounced ha.

You already know the article without realizing it: בַּבַּיִת (at home) is בְּ + הַ + בַּיִת, merged into a single word.

", "

The adjective follows the noun

In English, the adjective comes before the noun: \"a big house.\" In Hebrew it's the other way around, and it's simple: the adjective always comes after the noun, \"a house big.\" And it agrees in gender and number:

m. sg.f. sg.m. pl.f. pl.Meaning
גָּדוֹלגְּדוֹלָהגְּדוֹלִיםגְּדוֹלוֹתbig
קָטָןקְטַנָּהקְטַנִּיםקְטַנּוֹתsmall
יָפֶהיָפָהיָפִיםיָפוֹתbeautiful
נֶחְמָדנֶחְמָדָהנֶחְמָדִיםנֶחְמָדוֹתnice, friendly
בַּיִת גָּדוֹל, דִּירָה קְטַנָּה, חֲבֵרִים נֶחְמָדִיםa big house, a small apartment, nice friends [bayit gadol, dira ktana, khaverim nekhmadim]

With the article, the adjective takes it too: literally \"the house the big.\"

הַבַּיִת הַגָּדוֹל, הַדִּירָה הַקְּטַנָּהthe big house, the small apartment [ha-bayit ha-gadol, ha-dira ha-ktana]

English nouns have no gender, so learn each noun's gender along with the word: דִּירָה (an apartment) is feminine. And עִיר (city) is feminine even though it doesn't look it: עִיר גְּדוֹלָה.

", "

\"The house is big\" and זֶה / זֹאת / אֵלֶּה

Without the verb \"to be,\" everything depends on the article. Compare:

HebrewMeaningThe article
בַּיִת גָּדוֹלa big housenowhere
הַבַּיִת הַגָּדוֹלthe big houseon both words
הַבַּיִת גָּדוֹל.The house is big.only on the noun

To present something: זֶה (ze) before a masculine noun, זֹאת (zot) before a feminine noun, אֵלֶּה (ele) in the plural. Here too, no article: \"this is a…\"

זֶה חֶדֶר שָׁקֵט. זֹאת עִיר יָפָה. אֵלֶּה הַשְּׁכֵנִים.This is a quiet room. This is a beautiful city. These are the neighbors. [ze kheder shaket. zot ir yafa. ele ha-shkhenim]

Hebrew has no \"it\": for things, you say הוּא or הִיא depending on the noun's gender: הַחֶדֶר? הוּא קָטָן. (The room? It's small. Literally: \"he small.\") Remember: חֶדֶר is masculine in Hebrew.
